artworks.title: Aurora Taking Leave of Tithonus
artworks.description: Francesco Solimena's Aurora taking leave of Tithonus — the dawn goddess rising from the bed of her immortal, aging lover.

artworks.title: Aurora and Tithonus
artworks.description: Aurora and Tithonus — the gift of immortality without youth, the dawn forever leaving a diminishing husband.

artworks.title: Eos and Tithonos (kylix)
artworks.description: Eos and Tithonos on a kylix — archaic vase-painting of Dawn carrying off the Trojan prince.

artworks.title: Aurora and Tithonus
artworks.description: Giovanni da San Giovanni's Aurora and Tithonus — the immortal lover dwindling while Dawn rises forever young.

artworks.title: Eos
artworks.description: De Morgan's Eos — the dawn goddess whose gift of endless life without youth defines Tithonus' tragedy.

popCulture.title: Tithonus
popCulture.description: Eos' immortal but aging lover remains the caution of incomplete gifts — endless life without youth, and Tennyson's later elegy.
